body.statement: Using \(def:direct-calibration-handle\), determine the robust perturbation blocks, bounded-influence score, polynomial constants, and score-inversion critical value for which \(\widehat R_{\mathrm L}\) is measurable from \(\mathcal D_n\) and satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}Q_P^{(n)}\{|\widehat T_{\mathrm L}-E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\widehat T_{\mathrm L}|>\widehat R_{\mathrm L}\}\le\alpha/4\) together with \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\widehat R_{\mathrm L}]\lesssim_{\epsilon,\alpha}M\{n^{-1/2}+d/[n\log(en)]\}\). For every valid \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}_{n,b}\), the coefficient recurrence, factorial recurrence, outward score evaluation, and bisection in \(def:certified-finite-precision-algorithm\) must return a certified approximation to \(\widehat R_{\mathrm L}\) with absolute error at most \(\delta_{\mathrm{num}}/4\). The tail certificate must concern the selected marked-factorial statistic itself rather than a Markov conversion of its mean squared error, a cellwise union bound, or a generic median-of-means wrapper.
body.justification: This remains the central finite-sample inference obstruction for the selected marked-factorial statistic.
body.gap: The symmetric half-log score is nonmonotone and pilot-conditional centering does not control the unconditional target center.
body.consumer: A deployable rare-cell coverage certificate for saturated adjustment remains the intended consumer.

obligation.what_is_open: An explicit data-measurable rare-cell score interval with a direct tail event, sharp expected radius, pilot-centering control, and certified root inversion for the selected marked-factorial statistic.
obligation.obstruction: The stipulated symmetric half-log score is redescending, has zero derivative at \(\pm\sqrt2\), and can have multiple roots. The core also lacks a score controlling the random shift between the pilot-conditional and unconditional centers.
obligation.attempted: The exact derivative and a one-remote-block configuration were analyzed before any moment-generating-function step; they disprove monotone unique-root inversion for the proposed score. The banked bias result does not supply the missing tail or pilot-shift certificate.
obligation.partial_result:
The established node \(lem:four\text{-}coordinate\text{-}bias\) supplies the
bias \(C_\epsilon Md/[n\log(en)]\).  The stipulated score does not yet turn
this fact into the requested observable tail radius.  Indeed, for
\[
 \psi(x)=\frac12\log\frac{1+x+x^2/2}{1-x+x^2/2}
\]
one has
\[
 \psi'(x)=\frac{2(2-x^2)}{x^4+4}.
\]
Thus the score is increasing only on \((-\sqrt2,\sqrt2)\) and is decreasing
outside that interval.  For any odd block count \(B\ge3\), any \(\lambda>0\),
and block outputs \(Z_1=\cdots=Z_{B-1}=0\), \(Z_B=R/\lambda\), the proposed
score is
\[
 S_R(t)=-(B-1)\psi(\lambda t)+\psi(R-\lambda t).
\]
For sufficiently large \(R\), continuity and
\(\psi(x)\downarrow0\) as \(x\to\infty\) give
\[
 S_R(0)>0,\quad S_R(\sqrt2/\lambda)<0,\quad
 S_R((R-\sqrt2)/\lambda)>0,\quad S_R(R/\lambda)<0.
\]
Hence the zero equation has at least three roots.  A retained-range argument
could repair uniqueness, but no such range, positive slope modulus, or
pilot-centering correction is currently defined.
